text:
alex: Heads-up — seeing a spike in container eviction failures in us-west1 this morning. Root cause looks like NVMe devices hit readonly after a huge overlayfs fsync storm during container teardown. sample from node gnode-uw1-42:
```
Nov 30 08:17:03 gnode-uw1-42 kernel: nvme0: I/O 1024 queued, qdepth 127, sync_waiters 15
Nov 30 08:17:04 gnode-uw1-42 kernel: nvme0: critical_warning increased, metadata_errors=7
Nov 30 08:17:05 gnode-uw1-42 kernel: block nvme0 read latency 250ms
Nov 30 08:17:06 systemd: container-terminate: exit status 0
Nov 30 08:17:07 kernel: nvme0: device became read-only
```
alex: This coincided with a big provisioning window; GPUs couldn't be provisioned because scratch volumes were readonly, causing ~30 evictions.
priya: Do we see a cron or janitor job running at that time? also which firmware on the affected drives?

miguel: I pulled iostat and SMART counters from the impacted fleet subset. iostat shows read IOPS burst to ~135k for ~60s, avg r_await jumped. SMART: media_errors=0 but "available_spare" dipped slightly and "critical_warning" incremented 1->2 on 3 hosts. Devices are PM983-like variants, fw versions: 1.6.2 (most affected) vs 1.5.9 (less affected).
sasha: We rolled a runtime tweak last week that forces overlayfs to fsync on container exit for durability (CR: docker/ctr change). Also the ephemeral-cleaner cron runs a deep-compact every hour at :17 in us-west1 for older images. That lines up.
opsbot: deploy-bot: firmware-flash job completed for 120 nodes on Nov 28 02:10 UTC (fw=1.6.2).

alex: So likely combo: aggressive overlayfs fsync + concurrent deep-compact => transient queue saturation => controller changes qdepth handling and sets device readonly on error path.
priya: Immediate mitigations we can flip now: 1) throttle janitor compact concurrency in us-west1 to 2, 2) flip container runtime back to async-fsync-on-exit for hostpool `scratchpool-uw1`, 3) add temporary blkio throttle for the scratch cgroup to cap read IOPS to ~60k.
miguel: Commands to apply quick throttle (tested on canary):
```
# limit r_iops to 60000 for cgroup /scratchpool
cgcreate -g blkio:/scratchpool-temp
echo 60000 > /sys/fs/cgroup/blkio/scratchpool-temp/blkio.throttle.read_iops_device
# decrease janitor concurrency via k8s configmap
kubectl -n ops patch configmap/ephemeral-cleaner -p '{"data":{"concurrency":"2"}}'
# runtime flag rollback (systemd restart)
systemctl set-environment CONTAINER_FSYNC_ON_EXIT=false && systemctl restart containerd
```
sasha: I'll canary the throttle on 5 hosts and watch evictions. Also proposing a firmware canary rollback: reflash the 1.5.9 image on 10 nodes and observe if read-latency tails disappear. That would tell us if fw semantics changed qdepth behavior.
alex: Good. Can someone own running the immediate throttles and validating KPI (evictions, provision success rate, device readonly incidents)? We should also add a short-term alert: nvme0 read latency > 100ms x 30s -> notify eng-infra-pagers.
priya: I'll run the throttles and patch the configmap now. tagging @sasha to run the fw rollback canary and @miguel to gather SMART after changes. I'll post back in 10m with metrics.
oncall-bot: oncall:eng-infra acknowledged. Priority P2 — mitigation in progress.
alex: After we stabilize, follow-ups: a) change default container runtime behavior for teardown fsync to non-blocking, b) move deep-compact to off-peak window (+ jitter), c) drive vendor engagement for fw semantics around qdepth/recovery path, d) add a pre-emptive test that simulates overlayfs-fsync storms against a standby device to watch controller behavior.
priya: noted. I'll open a postmortem ticket and add the runbook steps. brief update in 15. :thumbsup:
